en.headline: Government to gazette sexual offences amendment bill on Friday
en.dek: The Security Bureau said the bill will modernise Hong Kong’s laws and strengthen victim protection, with first and second readings set for 25 November.
body: The government will publish the Sexual Offences Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026 in the Gazette on Friday, the Security Bureau said on Wednesday.

A spokesperson said the bill aims to strengthen protection for victims of sexual offences and to modernise Hong Kong’s laws so they keep pace with the times. Proposals cover non-consensual offences, offences involving children and persons with mental impairment, and other changes.

The government consulted the Legislative Council Panel on Security in July and received full support. A one-month public consultation from July to August drew 6,228 written submissions, of which 99.3 per cent expressed support. The bill incorporates feedback including a new offence for prolonged and repeated sexual abuse of children, and criminalisation of cyberflashing.
The bill will be introduced into the Legislative Council on 25 November for first and second readings. The government aims to complete the legislative exercise within the current term.

zh.headline: 政府周五刊憲性罪行修訂條例草案
zh.dek: 保安局表示草案將現代化香港性罪行法例並加強受害人保護，11月25日提交立法會首讀及二讀。
body: 政府將於星期五在憲報刊登《2026年性罪行法例（修訂）條例草案》，保安局周三表示。
發言人指，草案旨在加強對性罪行受害人的保護，並使香港的性罪行法例與時並進。建議涵蓋未經同意的性罪行、涉及兒童及精神缺損人士的罪行，以及其他修訂。
政府七月諮詢立法會保安事務委員會，獲得全面支持。七月至八月為期一個月的公眾諮詢共收到6228份書面意見，當中99.3%表示支持。草案採納了意見，包括引入處理持續及重複侵犯兒童的新罪行，以及刑事化網絡露體。
條例草案將於11月25日提交立法會進行首讀及二讀。政府目標在本屆任期內完成立法程序。
